targetReport.title: Council Regulation (EC) No 479/2009 on the application of the Protocol on the excessive deficit procedure
targetReport.description: The EDP Regulation — the instrument that turns the Treaty's excessive deficit procedure into a statistical reporting regime, and the second EU Regulation in this corpus to be modelled as a node after esa-2010. It matters here for Article 9, which compels into existence a published national document class that no other instrument this branch has followed produces: 'Member States shall provide the Commission (Eurostat) with a detailed inventory of the methods, procedures and sources used to compile actual deficit and debt data and the underlying government accounts' (Art. 9(1)), 'The inventories shall be updated following revisions in the methods, procedures and sources adopted by Member States' (Art. 9(3)), and 'Member States shall make their inventories public' (Art. 9(4)). Eurostat's own EDP inventories page states the consequence — 'Pursuant to Article 9 of Council regulation 479/2009 (as amended), all EU Member States are required to prepare and publish an EDP inventory' — and carries a live Inventory link for each of the 27. EUR-Lex titles it a '(Codified version)', codifying Council Regulation (EEC) No 3605/93. Note that the Regulation names no member state's inventory by title: AGENCY ONLY at exactly the point where a title would have produced a downward edge.
targetReport.cadence_note: Derived from an observed amendment record, not from a stated rate — see _open_questions. Adopted 25 May 2009; EUR-Lex lists exactly two consolidated versions, 19/08/2010 and 01/09/2014, with 01/09/2014 flagged as the current version. Two amendments across the 17 years to 2026.

release_schedule.note: April notification is provisional, October carries the revised annual figures. The underlying legal deadline (Reg. 479/2009 Art. 3(1)) is fixed at before 1 April and 1 October each year, so future cycles can be projected from that even without the exact transmission date.

targetReport.title: Frascati Manual — Guidelines for Collecting and Reporting Data on Research and Experimental Development
targetReport.description: OECD's standard for R&D statistics collection, cited by the EU's own R&D manual and, through it, by INSEE as the basis for French R&D expenditure statistics used in national accounts.

release_schedule.note: The Frascati Manual is a methodological guidelines document, not a periodic statistical release. Past editions were published in 1963, 1970, 1976, 1980, 1993, 2002, and 2015 (7th, current edition) — gaps between editions have ranged from 4 to 13 years, with no fixed cadence. OECD's own 'Continuing development of the OECD Frascati Manual' page and a 2024 NESTI document (DSTI/STP/NESTI(2024)3/REV2) explicitly state that NESTI 'does not envisage undertaking a wholesale revision of the Frascati Manual' at this time; instead it is producing supplementary 'complementary guidance' as an OECD Technical Paper annexed to the still-current 2015 edition. There is no calendar, no stated rule, and no consistent periodicity — the releases_per_year value of 0.2 (implying a 5-year cycle) does not match the actual historical pattern (roughly one edition every 8-13 years on average since 2002), and given the explicit 'no revision planned' statement, no fixed number is really appropriate here.

targetReport.title: 中华人民共和国预算法 (Budget Law of the People's Republic of China)
targetReport.publisher: 全国人民代表大会常务委员会 (Standing Committee of the National People's Congress)
targetReport.description: China's foundational budget statute, and the hub of this entire slice -- four separate documents in this corpus cite it by name in operative voice, which is what promotes it from BRICS/G.1's `deferred` note to a node. Enactment and amendment history, verbatim from the NPC's own page header: 「（1994年3月22日第八届全国人民代表大会第二次会议通过　根据2014年8月31日第十二届全国人民代表大会常务委员会第十次会议《关于修改〈中华人民共和国预算法〉的决定》第一次修正　根据2018年12月29日第十三届全国人民代表大会常务委员会第七次会议《关于修改〈中华人民共和国产品质量法〉等五部法律的决定》第二次修正）」. Commencement, 第一百零一条: 「本法自1995年1月1日起施行。1991年10月21日国务院发布的《国家预算管理条例》同时废止。」 The transfer-payment article, 第十六条, quoted in full because it is the statutory basis the whole Chinese fiscal-transfer chain rests on: 「国家实行财政转移支付制度。财政转移支付应当规范、公平、公开，以推进地区间基本公共服务均等化为主要目标。财政转移支付包括中央对地方的转移支付和地方上级政府对下级政府的转移支付，以为均衡地区间基本财力、由下级政府统筹安排使用的一般性转移支付为主体。按照法律、行政法规和国务院的规定可以设立专项转移支付，用于办理特定事项。建立健全专项转移支付定期评估和退出机制。市场竞争机制能够有效调节的事项不得设立专项转移支付。上级政府在安排专项转移支付时，不得要求下级政府承担配套资金。但是，按照国务院的规定应当由上下级政府共同承担的事项除外。」 ("The State implements a fiscal transfer payment system … with equalisation of basic public services across regions as the principal objective … with general transfer payments — used to equalise basic fiscal capacity across regions and arranged at the discretion of the lower-level government — as the main body…"). Also load-bearing for the central/local architecture, 第六条: 「中央一般公共预算包括中央各部门（含直属单位，下同）的预算和中央对地方的税收返还、转移支付预算。…中央一般公共预算支出包括中央本级支出、中央对地方的税收返还和转移支付。」 Fetched TIER A over plain HTTP from the NPC's own portal (HTTPS fails on that host with a ClientHello rejection -- see `_note`); completeness verified by confirming the extracted text runs from 第一条 through 第一百零一条, all 101 articles across 11 chapters.

results.basis: SOR/2007-303 s. 8(1)(y), the payroll-tax revenue base, makes SEPH a named term in a statutory formula: 'P is the gross dollar value, before deductions, of the payrolls of all employers in the province for the calendar year that ends in the fiscal year, as determined by Statistics Canada on the basis of its Survey of Employment, Payrolls and Hours, other than the payrolls of (i) employers not included in that survey, and (ii) employers in the following industry classifications, as defined by the North American Industry Classification System: (A) the elementary and secondary schools industry group, (B) the hospitals subsector, (C) the nursing and residential care facilities subsector, (D) the provincial and territorial public administration subsector, and (E) the local, municipal and regional public administration subsector'. `calculated_from` because P is a term in the formula, not a consideration — the same test that makes boc-bank-rate calculated_from the policy rate. Note the provision also carves out its own exclusions by NAICS classification, so the edge to `naics` is stated in the same sentence. SCOPE, stated because the section number alone overstates it: s. 8 sits in DIVISION 2 — Nova Scotia, and defines revenue base 'For the purpose of sections 3.71 to 3.9 of the Act', which are the Nova Scotia additional-equalization provisions. SEPH does NOT appear in the DIVISION 1 all-provinces revenue base at s. 5 — the phrase 'payrolls' occurs nowhere in ss. 1 through 8(1)(j), because the 2007 reform folded payroll taxes into the personal-income base. So this is the Equalization Program depending on SEPH through one division of the Regulations, not through the general formula.

targetReport.title: Council Regulation (EC) No 479/2009 on the application of the Protocol on the excessive deficit procedure
targetReport.description: The EDP Regulation — the instrument that turns the Treaty's excessive deficit procedure into a statistical reporting regime, and the second EU Regulation in this corpus to be modelled as a node after esa-2010. It matters here for Article 9, which compels into existence a published national document class that no other instrument this branch has followed produces: 'Member States shall provide the Commission (Eurostat) with a detailed inventory of the methods, procedures and sources used to compile actual deficit and debt data and the underlying government accounts' (Art. 9(1)), 'The inventories shall be updated following revisions in the methods, procedures and sources adopted by Member States' (Art. 9(3)), and 'Member States shall make their inventories public' (Art. 9(4)). Eurostat's own EDP inventories page states the consequence — 'Pursuant to Article 9 of Council regulation 479/2009 (as amended), all EU Member States are required to prepare and publish an EDP inventory' — and carries a live Inventory link for each of the 27. EUR-Lex titles it a '(Codified version)', codifying Council Regulation (EEC) No 3605/93. Note that the Regulation names no member state's inventory by title: AGENCY ONLY at exactly the point where a title would have produced a downward edge.
targetReport.cadence_note: Derived from an observed amendment record, not from a stated rate — see _open_questions. Adopted 25 May 2009; EUR-Lex lists exactly two consolidated versions, 19/08/2010 and 01/09/2014, with 01/09/2014 flagged as the current version. Two amendments across the 17 years to 2026.

targetReport.title: Statistics Act (Act No. 53 of 2007) — 統計法
targetReport.publisher: National Diet of Japan / Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications (MIC)
targetReport.description: Foundational statute that comprehensively reformed Japan’s official statistics system. Defines official statistics as information infrastructure, establishes fundamental statistics (基幹統計) and fundamental statistical surveys, creates the Statistics Commission, requires a Master Plan concerning the Development of Official Statistics, and sets rules for statistical surveys, confidentiality, secondary use, and coordination across the highly decentralised Japanese statistical system. Replaced the 1947 Statistics Act.
targetReport._notes:
Prime static + recurring-citation node — direct analogue of Mexico’s LSNIEG and Argentina’s Ley 17.622.

Article 1 states the purpose: ‘to promote systematic and efficient development of official statistics and to ensure the usefulness thereof through specifying basic matters concerning the production and provision of official statistics, and thereby to contribute to sound development of the national economy and enhancement of the living standards of the citizens.’

Official statistics are explicitly recognised as ‘information infrastructure’ usable not only by administration but by society as a whole. Fundamental statistics include the Population Census statistics, National Accounts, and other statistics designated by the Minister of Internal Affairs and Communications. Every subsequent methodological document, survey approval, and quality report cites the 2007 Act as the legal foundation. No independent publication cadence is required; continuous institutional citation satisfies the expanded node definition.

targetReport.title: International Standard Industrial Classification of All Economic Activities (ISIC)
targetReport.description: The United Nations' industry classification and the acknowledged parent of most national industrial classifications, including ANZSIC and its two predecessors. Its absence from this corpus was a hole of the same shape as the missing `gasb-standards` that the associated-states pass had to fill: `naics` was present with eight inbound edges while the classification NAICS itself is aligned to was not represented at all. Adopted 1948; revisions 1 (1958), 2 (1968), 3 (1990), 3.1 (2002), 4 (2007) and 5 (endorsed 2023, publication forthcoming).
targetReport.cadence_note: Six revisions in seventy-five years. Rev. 5 was endorsed by the UN Statistical Commission at its 54th session in 2023 and, as of this session's read of the UNSD page, is 'forthcoming' in published form while being distributed as introduction, explanatory notes and structure files. releases_per_year is nominal.

release_schedule.note: ISIC has no publication calendar or fixed revision cycle. Revisions occur irregularly and infrequently (Rev.3: 1989, Rev.3.1: 2002, Rev.4: 2008, Rev.5: endorsed by the UN Statistical Commission at its 54th session in March 2023). National adaptation of Rev.5 is targeted by 2025, business register updates by 2026, and statistical program implementation from 2027, but these are implementation milestones for the already-published Rev.5, not a future release date. The UN Committee of Experts on International Statistical Classifications recommended a five-year revision cycle for ISIC/CPC (raised at the 55th Statistical Commission session, 2024), but as of the 56th session (2025) documents, this had not been formally adopted -- a new Standing Task Team on ISIC and CPC was instead tasked with developing a revision-cycle strategy proposal. No computable next revision date exists yet.

targetReport.description: The annual indexation factor defined in section 44.2 of the Alberta Personal Income Tax Act and published each year by Treasury Board and Finance alongside the personal income tax bracket table.
